text:
alex: Draft PRD for the smart routing + fallback policy posted: https://redwood.internal/notes/PRD-1982 — TL;DR: tiered routing (premium/standard/best-effort), region affinity, and a fallback compatibility matrix for model variants. Need scope decision for MVP and clear acceptance criteria.

marta: skimmed — nice structure. my initial read: keep MVP small: tier routing + local-region fallback to a compatible variant. hold cross-region failover and cache warmup for v2.

cj: agree with MVP carve. two quick Qs: 1) do we require model-variant semantic compatibility (same tokenizer/width) for fallback, or allow output-transform? 2) how do we surface degraded-quality fallbacks to customers?

alex: answers: 1) MVP requires tokenization compatibility + similar generation params; we allow output-transform rules for specific repos (manual mapping). 2) surface via response header + telemetry event + optional user-visible warning for premium tiers.

ravi: from SRE/ops POV: acceptance criteria should include failover latency SLA and observability hooks. propose ACs: 
- AC1: fallback decision completes within 150ms for 95% of requests when primary unavailable.
- AC2: system emits fallback_event with reason and chosen variant.
- AC3: end-to-end p95 tail latency for premium not > 200ms overhead vs baseline when no failures.

lee: edge cases to call out: 
- incompatible kv-cache layouts when swapping variants mid-session;
- streaming sessions (how to reconnect/resume);
- function/tool-calling differences across variants.
We should add explicit abort/rollback rules for streaming.

product-ops: can we map these ACs to launch gates? i.e., must AC1-3 be green to GA for enterprise customers; for self-serve we could GA with AC2 only and feature-flag region failover.

alex: suggestion: launch plan: 
- internal dogfood (2 weeks) => ops/growth apps; must have AC2+observability and safe rollbacks.
- controlled GA to 10% of new signups => require AC1-2;
- full GA for paid enterprise => require AC1-3 + cross-region tests.

marta: scope negotiation note: deferring cross-region cache pre-warm reduces infra cost and complexity. we should add a tracking ticket for v2 heuristics (capacity-aware warmups, model transfer windows).

cj: propose acceptance test snippets (manual QA / e2e):
```
# simulate primary model down
POST /v1/generate {model: "redwood-xl-v1"}
-- assert fallback_event emitted
-- assert response.model == "redwood-xl-quant" or mapped variant
-- assert no tokenization errors
```

ravi: test infra TODO: chaotic failure injection (latency, OOM, model crashed) + replayed production traffic for 48h baseline. add to eng-sre backlog.

lee: for streaming we should add: if fallback requires new connection, return header `x-fallback-reconnect: true` and a minimal user-facing message chunk so apps can surface graceful degrade.

product-ops: P0 launch blockers from product side: clear docs for compatibility matrix, migration guide for customers pinning model versions, and a rollback runbook.

alex: action items: 
- alex: iterate PRD with ACs + add streaming rules (due EOD Thu).
- marta: write v2 tracker for cross-region warmup + heuristics (due next Tue).
- ravi: draft failure-injection tests + env estimates (due Mon).
- cj: add compatibility mapping examples + transform rules (due Wed).
- product-ops: outline launch gates and customer comm templates (due Fri).

deploy-bot: scheduled: canary rollout job queued for test-org on 1982-06-12 02:00 UTC :rocket: 

alex: thanks all — will post updated PRD link when done. reactions: :thumbsup: :eyes:
